rates_individual._note_qbi_rate_2026: OBBBA (P.L. 119-21 §70105) made §199A permanent at 20%. The 23% rate appeared only in the House-passed H.R. 1 and was NOT enacted — the rate is 20% for 2025, 2026 and later. From 2026 §70105 widens the phase-in ranges to $75,000 (non-joint) / $150,000 (joint) and adds a §199A(i) minimum deduction of $400 for taxpayers with at least $1,000 of aggregate active QBI.

qbi_threshold._note: Phase-in start. The single figure 201,775 is confirmed; the mfj figure follows the 32% bracket boundary (403,550) as it has in prior years, but one secondary source prints 403,500 - confirm against Rev. Proc. 2025-32 before relying on it.
qbi_threshold._note_obbba: OBBBA widens the phase-in RANGE from 2026: $75,000 non-joint / $150,000 joint, and adds the §199A(i) minimum deduction of $400 where aggregate active QBI is at least $1,000.

section_174_rd._note_obbba: OBBBA permanently restored §174 domestic R&D expensing. Foreign R&D remains 15-year capitalized. AUDIT FLASH POINT — confirm no further legislative changes.

rates_corporate._note_beat_rate_2026: OBBBA sets the §59A BEAT rate permanently at 10.5% for tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2025. The pre-OBBBA scheduled increase to 12.5% was not enacted.
rates_corporate._note_gilti_2026: OBBBA (§70321) sets the §250 deduction on NCTI (GILTI renamed "net CFC tested income") at 40% for tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2025 — effective rate 12.6% before the FTC haircut, which itself falls from 20% to 10%. The pre-OBBBA 37.5% sunset (13.125% effective) was not enacted.
rates_corporate._note_fdii_2026: OBBBA (§70321) sets the §250 deduction on FDDEI (FDII renamed "foreign-derived deduction eligible income") at 33.34% for tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2025 — effective rate approximately 14%. The pre-OBBBA 21.875% sunset (16.406% effective) was not enacted; the DTIR/QBAI routine-return construct is also removed.

transfer_taxes._note_nc_spouse: Rev. Proc. 2025-32: the IRC 2523(i)(2) annual exclusion for gifts to a non-citizen spouse rises to 194,000 for 2026, up 4,000 from 190,000 in 2025. Was null pending the revenue procedure.
transfer_taxes._note_estate_exclusion: OBBBA §70106 amended IRC §2010(c)(3) to set the basic exclusion amount at a flat $15,000,000 per person for decedents dying and gifts made after Dec 31, 2025, indexed for inflation after 2026. It is NOT the 2025 $13,990,000 figure carried forward and indexed — do not project ~$14.4M. The GST exemption under §2631(c) equals the basic exclusion amount, so it is also $15,000,000. The previously scheduled 2026 sunset to ~$7M is obsolete post-OBBBA.

_OBBBA_KNOWN_2026_CHANGES_SUMMARY: QBI deduction rate stays 20% — OBBBA made §199A permanent and did NOT enact the 23% House-bill rate; §199A phase-in ranges widen to $75,000/$150,000 and a $400 minimum deduction is added
§250 deduction on NCTI (renamed GILTI) drops from 50% to 40% (effective rate rises from 10.5% to 12.6%); deemed-paid FTC haircut falls from 20% to 10%
§250 deduction on FDDEI (renamed FDII) drops from 37.5% to 33.34% (effective rate rises from 13.125% to approximately 14%); DTIR/QBAI routine return removed
BEAT rate rises from 10% to 10.5% (permanent) — the pre-OBBBA 12.5% sunset was not enacted
§174 domestic R&D remains expensed (OBBBA permanent); foreign R&D still capitalized 15 years
Estate/gift exemption — TCJA sunset CANCELLED by OBBBA; remains at doubled level (indexed)
SALT cap indexes by 1% to ~$40,400; phaseout above $500k MAGI continues
§6041 information return threshold rises from $600 to $2,000
ARPA-enhanced PTC subsidies expire — reverts to pre-ARPA cliff unless extended
SECURE 2.0 Roth-only catch-up for high earners (>$145k) becomes mandatory
